traceability.evidence: Story file verification: - File docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md exists and its content matches the specification provided (same Acceptance Criteria, REQ-TEST-FIX-* requirements, Implementation Notes, Configuration Options, and Definition of Done).,Rule implementation – src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts: - Rule module is defined with meta.fixable: "code", enabling ESLint --fix as required by the story. - Options type and JSON schema include the story’s configuration options exactly as specified: - autoFixTestTemplate?: boolean (default true) - autoFixTestPrefixFormat?: boolean (default true) - testSupportsTemplate?: string - These options are wired into the rule: - ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate }) is called unconditionally for test files, handling file-level @supports insertion. - CallExpression visitor is built via handleCallExpression(context, { sourceCode, describeRegex, requireDescribeStory, requireTestReqPrefix, autoFixTestPrefixFormat }), connecting malformed-prefix fixes to it/test calls. - JSDoc traceability on the rule: - @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE confirms this rule explicitly implements this story’s requirements.,Helper implementation – src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts (file-level template): - buildSupportsTemplateComment(customTemplate?: string): - Uses a default baseTemplate string: "@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ". - Wraps it into a multi-line JSDoc block with an explicit TODO line: /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ - This matches the story’s template example shape and satisfies: - REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE (automatic @supports template for missing annotation), - REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER (clear placeholder text), - REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE (no attempt to infer real paths/IDs). - insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, customTemplate?): - Determines insertIndex at file start, but moves past a shebang line if present, preserving executable semantics. - Uses fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([insertIndex, insertIndex], templateComment) to insert only comment text. - Does not touch test implementation code, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE and REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE for file-level templates. - ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions): - Scans all comments for any @supports; if found, it does nothing (prevents duplicate templates). - If no @supports is present, reports messageId: "missingFileSupports". - Provides a fixer only when autoFixOptions.autoFixTestTemplate !== false, invoking insertSupportsTemplate with optional testSupportsTemplate override. - JSDoc on this helper includes @supports for Story 021.0 with REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.,Helper implementation – src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts (REQ prefix normalization): - normalizeReqId(raw: string): - Trims and uppercases the raw ID; requires it start with "REQ". - Removes leading separators after "REQ", converts internal whitespace/underscores to hyphens, collapses multiple hyphens. - Returns a canonical REQ-... string without generating new identifiers, implementing REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT while respecting REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE. - normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description: string): - If the description already matches canonical /^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/, returns null (no changes), preserving correctly formatted prefixes (REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE). - Handles malformed prefixes at the start of the string exactly as in the story’s Implementation Notes: - Square brackets with extra spacing: "[ REQ-XXX ]..." → "[REQ-XXX]...". - Underscore delimiter: "[REQ_XXX]..." → "[REQ-XXX]...". - Parentheses: "(REQ-XXX)..." → "[REQ-XXX]...". - Lowercase: "[req-xxx]..." → "[REQ-XXX]...". - Only operates when a REQ-like token starts the string; otherwise returns null, so it never invents prefixes (REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE). - createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(originalNode, newValue, sourceCode): - Reads the raw literal text from sourceCode.getText(originalNode). - Preserves the original quote character (' / " / `) and escapes backslashes and embedded quotes appropriately. - Falls back to JSON.stringify for non-standard literal forms. - This ensures only the literal’s content changes while code structure and quoting are preserved, meeting REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE. - handleItOrTestCall(context, node, description, options): - Applies only when requireTestReqPrefix is true (configurable as per story). - If description does not start with a canonical [REQ-...] pattern: - Computes normalizedDescription using normalizeReqPrefixInDescription when autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false. - Always reports messageId: "missingReqPrefix" (validation behavior from Story 020.0). - Attaches a fixer only when all of the following are true: - autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false, - normalizedDescription !== null (i.e., the string contained a recognizable REQ ID), - first argument is a string Literal. - The fixer replaces only that literal via createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw. - This logic ensures: - REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT: malformed-but-recognizable prefixes are normalized. - REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE: no fix is produced when there is no recognizable REQ ID. - REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE: only the name string changes, not surrounding code. - REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE: missing prefixes result in an error without any auto-generated ID.,Visitor wiring – src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts: - handleCallExpression(context, options) returns a CallExpression visitor used in require-test-traceability.ts: - Uses getCalleeName + isTestCallName to process describe/it/test/context only (framework integration from Story 020.0). - For describe, delegates to handleDescribeCall, which only validates description content and never auto-adds story references, matching the story’s "Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE" list. - For it/test, delegates to handleItOrTestCall, where malformed-prefix normalization and safe auto-fixing occur. - JSDoc on handleCallExpression declares @supports for Story 021.0 with REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE, reinforcing traceability.,Tests – tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts (covers Story 021.0 behavior explicitly): - File header JSDoc: - @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE directly links all Story 021.0 requirements to this test file. - Valid case for safe behavior: - A test where @supports is present and the test name uses a correct [REQ-TRACE-123] prefix verifies that correctly formatted names are not modified, supporting REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE and REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE. - Invalid case – file-level template insertion (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE / REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER / REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE / REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE): - Input code (no @supports): describe('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', () => { it('[REQ-ONE] works', () => {}); }); - Expected output: /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ describe(...) - Confirms ESLint --fix inserts a placeholder JSDoc at the file top, with clear TODO guidance and unchanged test body. - Invalid case – missing REQ prefix (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE, Error Handling): - Code has valid @supports but it('missing prefix', ...) with no [REQ-...] prefix. - Test expects errors: [{ messageId: "missingReqPrefix" }] and does NOT specify an output, verifying no auto-fix is applied when a prefix is absent (no inference of IDs). - Invalid cases – malformed prefix normalization (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE): - Spacing: '[ REQ-TEST-FIX ] does something' → '[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something'. - Underscore: '[REQ_TEST_FIX] does something' → '[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something'. - Lowercase: '[req-lowercase] bad casing' → '[REQ-LOWERCASE] bad casing'. - Parentheses: '(REQ-PAREN) with parens' → '[REQ-PAREN] with parens'. - Each test specifies both code and expected output strings, proving the exact transformations described in the story’s Implementation Notes.,Targeted test run for this story – Jest: - Command executed: npm test -- --runInBand --verbose tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - Output: - PASS tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - All 11 tests in this suite passed, including those that verify: - File-level @supports template insertion for missing annotations. - Normalization of malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes (spacing, underscores, lowercase, parentheses). - No auto-fix when a REQ prefix is completely missing. - Confirms the current implementation of Story 021.0 behavior is tested and passing.,Documentation – user-docs/api-reference.md (user-facing docs for this story): - traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements from docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md are fully implemented and verified: - File-level @supports templates with clear TODO placeholders are automatically inserted for test files missing annotations, controlled by autoFixTestTemplate and testSupportsTemplate (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE). - Malformed [REQ-XXX] test-name prefixes are normalized exactly as specified (spacing, underscores, parentheses, case), only when an existing REQ ID is present, and without inventing new IDs (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE). - Implementation uses ESLint’s fixer API with meta.fixable: "code" and carefully scoped fixes that do not alter test implementation code, preserving structure and formatting. - RuleTester tests explicitly cover template insertion, malformed-prefix correction, and the no-inference behavior; they all pass in the current codebase. - User-facing API documentation describes these auto-fix behaviors and configuration options in detail.
Based on the current repository state and passing tests, this story is fully implemented and meets its Definition of Done.
